statement: Authorship, planning, orchestration, and final or gating judgment remain on the primary provider; only cheap fan-out judging can route local.
verdict: Policy classification, not a local-model accuracy measurement.

statement: Among multi-lens reviewers, only the Style lens is treated as a cheap local slice; Correctness and Bugs remain on the primary provider.

statement: Judge arms requiring live tools such as WebFetch, browser, gh, or substrate commands must remain on the primary provider.

statement: A local judge array is allowed only when a strong-tier provider gate consolidates it; directly gating arrays remain disabled until that gate exists.
verdict: Safety invariant, not a benchmarked accuracy threshold.

statement: build-step-style is a standing disabled call site because the surrounding Step 7 merge decision must not admit a local model.

statement: A large cross-cutting plan-feature is a conditional Fable escalation case.
verdict: Named policy trigger; no comparative quality study attached.

statement: A high-stakes substrate or schema review-deep bugs lens is a conditional Fable escalation case.
verdict: Named policy trigger; no comparative quality study attached.

statement: A cross-memory latent-principle consolidation round in memory-distill is a conditional Fable escalation case.
verdict: Named policy trigger; the claimed quality comparison remains unmeasured.

statement: Parallel fan-out arms remain Sonnet-tier because their value is diversity, not stronger per-arm reasoning.
verdict: Policy rationale; the A3 arm experiment is the only direct paired evidence in this ledger.

statement: Single-mind synthesis must not be fanned out merely to avoid choosing whether a stronger model is warranted.
verdict: Policy rationale, not a measured synthesis-quality result.

statement: A conditional Fable escalation is incomplete unless it names a concrete trigger rather than relying on subjective size.
verdict: Policy completeness rule, not a measurement.

statement: A session escalation that fans out work is actionable only when the dispatched arms are explicitly pinned to Sonnet; otherwise it must carry an arms-unpinned warning.
verdict: Policy and incident-derived safeguard; quality effect is not separately benchmarked.

statement: The historical assertion that memory-distill is slightly worse on Fable is not supported by a quality measurement and must remain an assertion.
verdict: Explicitly recorded as an assertion dressed as evidence in the seed reconnaissance.

statement: The paired A3 run supports keeping Sonnet arms pinned for deep research because it showed no decision-changing gross quality gap against the fully Fable-armed baseline.
verdict: KEEP Sonnet arms pinned; n=1 versus n=1 and drift-confounded, so it only rules out a gross gap.
preregistration: Finding-overlap plus spot-check accuracy of the Sonnet-arm report versus the Fable-arm baseline on the same question decides whether Sonnet arms stay pinned for deep research.

statement: The fully Fable-armed deep-research baseline exposed a cost and reliability failure that motivates pinning fan-out arms to Sonnet.
verdict: Operational cost and reliability evidence only; it does not establish a quality advantage.

statement: Switchboard's cold and warm timeout defaults and token floor are backed by observed endpoint timing and reasoning-token behavior, not by local-slice quality measurements.
verdict: Operational endpoint profile only; it cannot prove a slice is safe to offload.
